title: CABAL: Multi-Agent Simulacra for Tracing the Effects of Collusive Bidding in Peer Review
abstract: arXiv:2609.05227v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Recent reports during the AAAI-27 review cycle highlight the risk of reviewers coordinating bids for reciprocal assignment advantage. Prior work treats bidding, reviewer assignment, and review manipulation as separate stages, leaving the lifecycle effects of collusive bidding unclear. Real-world analysis is further constrained by typically unobservable collusive intent and the lack of counterfactuals for the same conference. Motivated by this gap, we introduce \alg, an end-to-end multi-agent simulacra framework for studying reviewer assignment integrity by holding the conference environment fixed and configuring LLM-driven reviewer agents with honest or collusive policies. We further develop an affinity-guided collusive bidding strategy that uses mutual reviewer-paper affinities to construct collusion rings and select target papers, producing expertise-consistent rather than arbitrarily targeted attacks. translated_title: CABAL：用于追踪同行评审中合谋投标影响的多智能体仿真框架
translated_abstract: AAAI-27评审周期期间的最新报告凸显了审稿人通过协调投标以获取互惠分配优势的风险。先前的工作将投标、审稿人分配和评审操纵视为相互独立的阶段，导致合谋投标在整个流程中的生命周期效应尚不清楚。现实世界的分析进一步受到限制，因为合谋意图通常无法被观察到，且缺乏针对同一会议的反事实对照。基于这一研究空白，我们提出了CABAL，一个端到端的多智能体仿真框架，用于研究审稿人分配的完整性：该框架通过固定会议环境，并配置由大语言模型驱动的、采用诚实或合谋策略的审稿人智能体来进行实验。我们进一步开发了一种亲和力引导的合谋投标策略，该策略利用审稿人与论文之间的相互亲和力来构建合谋圈子并选择目标论文，从而产生与专业领域一致而非任意针对性的攻击。受控实验表明……
tldr: 提出了端到端多智能体仿真框架CABAL，通过为LLM审稿人智能体配置诚实或合谋策略来研究同行评审中合谋投标的影响，并设计了基于审稿人-论文亲和力的合谋投标策略，实现与专业领域一致而非任意的定向攻击。
